recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. If BR&R wants a direct reference from a subject state transition to a causal AdverseEvent, handle that as a new change request because the published R5 implementation and later R6 approvals use coded state-change reasons rather than a Reference choice.
issue_request: FHIR-23028 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification BR&R change request asking for a way to track why a ResearchSubject discontinued from a study and potentially connect that reason to an AdverseEvent; the accepted path was fuller subject lifecycle status/progress information.
initial_application: ResearchSubject.progress was added historically in afae9447904fefafb8605fbe0786232a4fdd7c89, and e25dc63817146f6e664114198b526b775941a3fa explicitly mentioned Jira #23028 as adding progress during R5 ResearchSubject preparation. The R5 published profile had ResearchSubject.status as publication status and ResearchSubject.progress with subjectState, milestone, reason, startDate, and endDate.
additional_context: FHIR-31657 later approved the already-balloted ResearchSubject progress/current-state implementation and resolved the process concern noted in FHIR-23028 comments. BR&R minutes for 2021-03-30 record a 16-0-0 motion to add ResearchSubject.CurrentState. Later Applied R6 issues FHIR-43561 and FHIR-44837 replaced the R5 progress backbone with subjectState and subjectMilestone and define reason as CodeableConcept.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current ResearchSubject is active in the build, status is publication status, subjectState carries code/startDate/endDate/reason, subjectMilestone carries milestone/date/reason, and source/fhir.ini maps the old R5 progress elements to the current R6 structures.
